text: Yes, the two directions of the same frames. MERGE: many streams into one connection, which is the multiplexing itself (a node's uploads, chats and files share one link). FAN: one stream out to many receivers. The sender uploads each frame once, and the relay copies it to every subscriber on its turn (a live video to ten viewers costs the sender one upload, not ten). Both use the same frames and the same turn-taking, so fan-out needs no new mechanism, only a stream that has more than one receiver.

wsl-claude: yes, the two halves. MERGE is many streams into one connection (what each end's multiplexer does). FAN is one stream out to many receivers: you send a song or a group call ONCE to the relay, and the relay copies each frame to every listener, so your home line uploads once however many are listening. One thing to settle with it: a fanned stream costs the relay once per listener going out, not once. So the owner's ceiling has to count the copies, or one broadcast to a hundred listeners quietly takes the whole box. Fairness then means per member, including what their fan-outs cost.

Right, the relay already has half of it. Its SSE streams are the FAN side: one stream out to each member, carrying whatever is addressed to them. What's missing is the MERGE side on the way IN: today each upload is one whole post, answered and done. A streaming post would arrive as frames, and the relay would MERGE them, taking turns member by member, into the SSE stream of whoever they're for. So an upload stream in, turned into frames interleaved into the receiver's existing stream out. The receiving side barely changes; the relay's inbound side is the new part.

wsl-claude: right, and the tree confirms it. The relay already fans over SSE: presentNow.broadcast sends one event to every present member (relay.js:1290 partner, :1926 route, :2585 presence), and presentNow.send delivers to one member's stream (:2321 requests, :2990 replies). So the DOWNSTREAM half of streaming is already there: each member's SSE stream can carry frames too, interleaved with everything else it carries today. What's missing is only the UPSTREAM mirror, a streaming POST from each member into the relay, where the relay MERGES frames from many senders and schedules them onto the right receivers' SSE streams, turn by turn. That keeps the streams goal small: one new direction, and the scheduler between them.

Yes: one loop, a switch. Each turn, it takes the next ready frame from each incoming connection in turn, looks up where that frame's stream goes, and puts it on the outgoing connection of each receiver, which is one for a plain stream and many for a fan. It never holds more than a frame per stream, so memory stays flat however big the transfers are, and the routing decision is made once, when a stream opens, not per frame.
